key_insight: In surgically repaired congenital heart disease, true gaps in cardiology follow-up are common and are often driven by insurance and social instability rather than clinical need.
clinical_relevance: Missed follow-up can lead to silent disease progression, urgent interventions, and serious morbidity or mortality even in patients with simple CHD.
method: Retrospective cohort of 1,746 patients with surgically repaired CHD at a tertiary center (2003–2020).
Used EMR data plus manual chart review to separate true gaps in care from appropriate follow-up patterns.
Assessed factors linked to gaps in care and outcomes after return to care.
evidence_signal: After chart review, 275 patients (15.7%) had true gaps in care; 41.5% returned to care, and 13% of those returning needed intervention, with 26.7% of intervened patients experiencing major morbidity or mortality.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data may limit generalizability, and documentation gaps could underestimate social drivers or outcomes.
paper_title: Gaps in Congenital Heart Disease Care: Social Drivers and Clinical Consequences
